comments.author: Ved Vekhande
comments.comment: The part people skip is calibrating the judge on failures, not just good answers. I usually want the first 30 labels to include obvious passes, obvious fails, borderline cases, and cases where the model sounds right but violates the task.

comments.author: Daniel T.
comments.comment:
The real security boundary for coding agents is not “can they talk?” - it is “what authority does a received message carry?”

I like the pattern of treating remote agent output as quoted, untrusted text. That maps better to how prompt injection actually works: most failures start when plain text silently becomes instruction.

Sharp question: do you see teams wanting repo-scoped agent-to-agent messaging, or task-scoped messaging that expires when the branch/PR is done?

#AgenticAI #LLMOps

comments.author: 구우영
comments.comment: The line between “I wrote it” and “my agent wrote it” gets clearer when you track who made the irreversible decisions: framing, tradeoffs, taste, and what to leave out. The agent can draft words, but the author is still the person accountable for the judgment behind them.

comments.author: Haus der KI
comments.comment: The best AI vocabulary often shows up at the boundary between policy, architecture, and workflow, not inside model docs. One term I had to revisit recently was “data residency” because in agent systems it changes from a compliance checkbox into an actual design constraint.
